description: This bar chart, from the paper "Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models," illustrates the mean effect sizes (with error bars indicating standard deviation) for six different morphosyntactic tags—'case', 'gender', 'number', and 'tense'—across six multilingual BERT model variants: mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂. The horizontal axis, labeled 'tag', presents the four morphosyntactic categories in order from left to right. The vertical axis, labeled 'effect', is scaled linearly from 0 to 20, with tick marks at regular intervals of 5. Each tag category contains a group of six bars, one for each model variant, color-coded according to the legend in the top right corner: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). For the 'case' tag, the bars show a clear trend where mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ have the highest effect values, approximately 12 and 11 respectively, while the others are lower, with mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂ around 6 and mBERT-R₂ and XLM-R₂ around 3. For 'gender', the effect sizes are generally smaller, with mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ around 4, and the others below 3. For 'number', the effect sizes are even smaller, with all models showing values below 3, and for 'tense', all bars are near zero, with mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ showing the smallest non-zero values, approximately 0.5. The bars are not sorted by height; they are presented in the order of the model variants as listed in the legend. The error bars extend above and below each bar, indicating the variability of the effect size.
